assertion_analysis.failure_condition: Reddens on the declared regression: with `EOFError` removed from cli.py:2466's tuple, `gzip.decompress` raises out of `_engine_running_requests` and the test errors at its `is None` assertion - <run>/negative-control.log records exactly this as `1 failed ... EOFError: Compressed file ended before the end-of-stream marker was reached`. The expected `None` is a constant the test supplied, not a value derived from the body it passed in, so it is not self-comparing.

Reddens if `zlib.error` alone is removed from cli.py:2466: the corrupt deflate body raises `zlib.error` out of the reader instead of returning None. The node's declared control removed both exception names together, so this test's own half of the tuple is not isolated by the control, though it would redden on that mutation.

Reddens only against the pair: with both reload.py:119 and cli.py:2466 reverted the exception propagates out of run_overlap and `result.outcome == "reloaded"` fails. With cli.py:2466 alone reverted it stays green, as the node's negative-control note states, so it does not guard reload.py:119 in isolation - see the first finding. `world.now == 600` and `old_drain_timed_out is True` are independent of the injected body; they assert the drain polls to its bound rather than aborting.

Reddens on reverting imas_ambix/agent/lane.py:534-536: restoring `raise ValueError("engine metrics carry no valid running-request count")` makes `lane.fetch_lane_capacity(...).running == 0` raise rather than compare, and the test errors. The expected `0` is a literal, not the value the test handed in, and no independent source could move with it, so it is not self-comparing.

findings.text: follow-on: the widened `except (OSError, ValueError, EOFError, zlib.error)` at imas_ambix/agent/reload.py:119 is covered by no test that reddens when it alone regresses. The node's own negative-control note on the reviewed manifest records this: removing `EOFError, zlib.error` from the reader's tuple still leaves `test_truncated_gzip_scrape_keeps_the_drain_waiting_to_its_bound` green, because cli.py:2466 returns None before the overlap guard sees anything, and every production caller reaches run_overlap through that reader (imas_ambix/agent/cli.py:2686). A future edit that narrows reload.py's tuple back to `(OSError, ValueError)` therefore passes the whole gate. The guard is genuine defence in depth against any read_old_running that raises, but it is asserted nowhere, so durability for that half of repair (1) rests on the reader alone.

follow-on: the same decode failure the node repaired escapes the lane publisher's handler one call site over. `_publish_lane` catches `(aiohttp.ClientError, OSError, RuntimeError, ValueError)` around `asyncio.to_thread(fetch_lane_capacity, ...)` at imas_ambix/agent/router.py:2138, and EOFError and zlib.error are neither (confirmed: `issubclass(EOFError, OSError)` is False). So a truncated-gzip or corrupt-deflate scrape raises out of the loop and ends the publisher task, where its own docstring at imas_ambix/agent/router.py:2105 says every failure publishes an explicit unavailable state and the loop continues. This is pre-existing and outside the node's declared write paths (router.py is not in its scope), and the node's change does not make it reachable — fetch_lane_capacity has raised these since it decoded inline — so it does not hold this node. It is recorded because it is the identical defect at the boundary whose fetch contract the node explicitly left as a follow-on, and it costs one tuple entry to close.
